item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) and New Orleans Pelicans guard Jeremiah Fears (0) get into an altercation during the second quarter of an NBA game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) PORTLAND, Ore. - Victor Wembanyama missed his first game of the season Monday in Sacramento. De'Aaron Fox missed his second. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson saw a silver lining in the former absence. The latter was another matter. Fox was sidelined with a right shin contusion suffered two nights earlier against New Orleans, on a play Johnson believed crossed the line. With 46 seconds remaining in the first quarter of Saturday's 114-91 victory over the Pelicans , Fox was cutting through the lane when Jeremiah Fears stuck out a leg and struck the All-Star guard in the shin. "From my perspective, it looked like he got tripped," Johnson said. "I wasn't a huge fan of seeing that play when it happened on tape. Now he has to miss a game because of it." Johnson indicated the Spurs have submitted video of the play to the NBA office for review, though further disciplinary action appears unlikely. With Fox out and guard Dylan Harper missing his third consecutive game with a hip strain, the Spurs opted to keep Wembanyama sidelined against the Kings as well. The official designation for Wembanyama's ailment was "lower back tightness." His absence allowed the Spurs to work on what has been their greatest weakness during a 15-3 start to the season - learning how to function when their All-Star center is off the floor. item.title: The USMNT needs Copa América. What it doesn't need is another home game
item.description: USA fans look on from the stands during the CONMEBOL Copa America match between the United States and Boliva on June 23, 2024 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Copa América, South American soccer’s pride and joy, is returning to the U.S. in 2028 because organizers remain spellbound by the ticket sales and marketing success of the 2024 edition here. Tuesday’s announcement is a positive development for the U.S. team, which, for competitive reasons, desperately needs a break from the monotony of CONCACAF before the 2030 World Cup. Only so much is gained from fiddling with neighbors over and over again. Assuming the U.S. qualifies next summer, Copa América will furnish its to-be-announced head coach with pressure-packed, consequential matches in a prestigious tournament against different types of opponents. That’s a welcome change from the Nations Leagues and biennial Gold Cups, which are starting to feel like watching “Friends” reruns on Nick at Nite. But here’s where this Copa news falls short for the U.S. program: It’s in the U.S. again. Yes, the team needs to play in Copa América, but what it really needs is to play in it in South America. It needs to step out of its comfort zone of sterile hotels and stadiums. It needs to say goodbye to family and friends, experience new training and playing environments, and feel the heat of stepping into Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã or Buenos Aires’ El Monumental to play the host team. True, the U.S. often feels like the visiting team at home when it tangles with Latin American opponents boasting a passionate diaspora. But the players still enjoy the predictability of home logistics, travel patterns, security and general nationwide support. That is not what they need right now. They need to suffer. Consider this: The U.S. hardly ever plays outside its borders, an arrangement that many might argue has left the program soft heading into World Cups. Talent, tactics and such are part of why the U.S. has stumbled in the round of 16 in its past four appearances, but mental toughness in the pressure-cookers of knockout soccer can’t be dismissed either. The location of matches is often out of the U.S.’s control. For revenue purposes, CONCACAF has staged every Nations League final four and almost every Gold Cup in the States. CONMEBOL, which oversees South American soccer, has shifted Copa América — the oldest international tournament in the world — to the U.S. three of the past five times after staging the first 44 editions in its own continent. The U.S. does have a say in the location of friendlies. Here again, though, the team is not facing the rigors of playing away matches. It has played 16 consecutive friendlies in FIFA windows at home since a visit to Mexico in October 2024. Going back to 2022, the number grows to 28 of 31. item.title: Scarlett Schremmer Disqualified From Annika Debut After Lying
item.description: Michael Madrid-Imagn Images The 19-year-old University of Miami sophomore received a rare sponsor exemption to The Annika driven by Gainbridge, only to disqualify herself by lying about a yardage book. She claimed she never used the illegal green-reading material when officials first asked, but photographic evidence proved otherwise. Golfmagic reported the disqualification came Saturday after the tour saw clear images of her consulting the prohibited book during the round. The book itself was legal in college golf, which explains why it sat in her bag, but it carries zero weight on the professional tour. Schremmer missed the cut before the ruling dropped, yet the lie turned a missed opportunity into a scandal. Her mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, caddied for her, adding a layer of personal pressure that clearly backfired. Social media saw playing partner Perrine Delacour publicly challenge the tournament’s rule breach handling, causing the situation to become messy. The Lie That Sealed Her Fate Officials were alerted to the issue after the opening round, yet Schremmer kept playing on Friday before the truth came out. She initially told officials the book was not in use, a claim she later admitted was false in a Friday Instagram post. Schremmer wrote, “I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal Information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use.” That panic cost her the chance to show her skills against the best women in the world. Delacour, who partnered Schremmer for the first two rounds, took to X to ask, “Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies.” The French veteran confirmed she spoke directly to rules officials about the violation, highlighting how the amateur status of the invitee complicated the situation. The LPGA Tour stated the rule requires players to use only approved books throughout their round, and photo evidence showed Schremmer violated that mandate. Trust Is Hard To Build Back With two fall college tournament wins and a USGA 2026 Elite Amateur Program spot secured, Schremmer held the 51st rank in the World Amateur Golf Ranking. Those credentials meant nothing once she chose to hide the truth. While Schremmer’s Friday admission signaled a move from denial to accountability, the harm remains irreversible. She stated in her post, according to Yahoo, “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

item.title: 'Go be somewhere else': Steelers legend challenges DK Metcalf
item.description: Credit: The Pivot Sports After a strong start to the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have lost back-to-back games coming off the bye, and star receiver DK Metcalf is once again sucking up oxygen around the team in on-field confrontations. During Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Metcalf was ejected for poking Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. The incident came after key drops and a build-up of physicality with the Philadelphia secondary throughout the game. Metcalf had just one reception for 2 yards, his third time in the past four contests with two or fewer catches. The former Seahawk is set to make $38-plus million starting next season, putting a glaring spotlight on his lack of productivity and professionalism and leading former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin to check Metcalf on Sunday Night Football after the ejection. During an episode of The Pivot Sports to start the week, fellow Steelers great Ryan Clark added to the criticism of Metcalf, calling out the star for his lack of “emotional regulation” and questioning whether Metcalf was long for Pittsburgh. “Why do we have to be the guy that can’t control himself? That has no professional maturity. That doesn’t understand emotional regulation,” Clark said. “Then you get disqualified, and you shake your head.” Clark showed several of Metcalf’s earlier miscues in the game, contrasting the star’s lack of focus with how his backup, Max Hurleman, played as well as the clutch performance of Philadelphia’s DeVonta Smith on the other side. Clark emphasized how much Metcalf’s mistakes cost the team. “Maybe throw hands when you’re getting locked up. Maybe throw hands when you’re trying to get a block. Maybe throw hands when it’s 3rd-and-4, and you need to get four yards. But you want to do it after the play?” Clark said. “Slapping the referee, that doesn’t make you a bad man. That makes you a man that eventually goes home.” The incident with DeJean also opened Metcalf and the Steelers up to media chatter and off-field distractions . Later, Clark highlighted numerous Steelers greats from the team’s two Super Bowl runs in the late 2000s and early 2010s, challenging Metcalf to match their mental toughness and leadership. “Most of the games, they were all available. And what they did was lead,” he said. “They would never walk out on their team after being kicked out of a game, without hearing what the coach had to say, without hearing what their teammates had to say. Be accountable, DK. Lead, DK. Be the person that they brought you over there to be. And if not, go be somewhere else.” To make matters worse for the Steelers, after acquiring Metcalf, the team ultimately turned him into the replacement for former Pittsburgh draft pick George Pickens. item.title: Tsunami RT Brings Porsche To IMSA GTD Class For 2027 Season
item.description: Manthey racing�s Porsche 911 (911) is a blur of speed up from turn 5 during practice at the Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix Featuring IMSA, Friday, July 31, 2026, at Road America near Elkhart Lake, Wis. Tsunami RT is heading to the United States to race. The San Marino-based team will field a Porsche 911 GT3 R in the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup starting in 2027. This move brings a new name to the GTD class and adds depth to the five-race schedule. Team principal Valerio M. Speziali wants to build a lasting presence in North America. He sees the US market as a place to grow the team’s skills over time. “We are delighted to join the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup next year, giving us the chance to build our experience and grow in endurance racing season by season,” Speziali said, according to Speedway Digest . The group knows the competition is fierce, but they are not backing down. “We know how competitive the GTD field is and we’re ready to fight for strong results from the opening round,” he added according to Speedway Digest. A Driver Mix Built for Endurance The car will carry the number 79 and feature a mix of veterans and fresh talent. Fabio Babini leads the group with deep roots in IMSA history. He won the GTU class at the 2000 Rolex 24 and took the GT title at Le Mans in 2001. His last start in the WeatherTech Championship was back in 2019, but he knows the track well. Matteo Cressoni brings recent experience with 13 starts between 2015 and 2025 in various GT cars. Two new faces will make their debut in 2027. Alex Fontana and Johannes Zelger have raced together for Tsunami RT in the Intercontinental GT Challenge during the 2026 season. The team will rotate drivers based on the race length. They plan to use a three-driver lineup for the Sebring, Glen, Road America, and Road Atlanta events. This strategy helps manage the physical toll of long races while keeping speed high. Adding a new Porsche entry changes the dynamic of the GTD class. The field is already crowded with top-tier teams, and every new car adds pressure. Babini’s resume shows the team is not just playing for participation. He has won at the highest levels of sports car racing. His experience in the GRAND-AM series and American Le Mans Series gives the team a solid foundation. Cressoni has also seen action in Ferrari and Lamborghini entries, proving he can handle different machines. The Rolex 24 holds special weight for this organization. Speziali called the chance to see the team on the entry list a major milestone. It is not just about finishing the race. It is about proving that a European team can succeed in the tough US endurance scene. The 2027 season will show if they have the pace to match the big names. According to Speedway Digest, the 2027 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship will mark Tsunami RT’s debut with a Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) competing across the five-race IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup schedule.

item.description: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is ready to return after missing five games with an issue that continued bothering him during Edmonton’s recent road trip. The Edmonton Oilers forward addressed his absence before facing the Vegas Golden Knights . Speaking to NHL reporters, Nugent-Hopkins explained that something happened near the end of Edmonton’s game in Toronto. He spent the following week dealing with the problem before the team cleared him to return. “I feel good now. Something kind of happened near the end in Toronto, and just kind of was battling that all week and dealing with that,” Nugent-Hopkins said . MORE: NHL analyst Elliotte Friedman defends cancer survivor after Canadian anthem mishap He also suggested the issue might have started with an earlier puck impact. “Maybe it led from a couple weeks ago with the puck, but just stuck around on the road on a long road trip, not playing any games,” he added. item.description: Dave Portnoy on the sideline before kickoff of the first half between Michigan and Oklahoma at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026. The University of Michigan announced Tuesday that, despite earlier reports that it had landed Trev Alberts as its next athletic director, it ultimately decided not to proceed with the hire. “The University of Michigan’s search for its next athletic director is ongoing,” Michigan spokesperson Paul Corliss said in a statement. “As we navigate a rapidly changing landscape in intercollegiate athletics, the values that define Michigan will guide our decisions and reinforce our commitment to excellence and integrity, both in the classroom and in competition.” Michigan’s regents reportedly decided that Alberts wasn’t the right choice after immersing themselves in the details of a 2024 lawsuit at Nebraska involving an inappropriate relationship between a basketball coach and a player. However, Alberts had already signed a binding MOU and will receive a $17.3 million from the school. item.title: Blue Jays land Japanese star pitcher Kaima Taira on $80M deal
item.description: Blue Jays signing The Blue Jays landed a starting pitcher for roughly one-sixth the price of Tarik Skubal. After losing to the Mets in the Skubal sweepstakes, the Blue Jays pivoted and are signing Japanese righty Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million deal, The Post’s Jon Heyman first reported . The deal includes an opt-out clause after the third year, per Heyman. Kaima Taira of the Seibu Lions celebrates setting an NPB record with 39 consecutive scoreless games in Fukuoka, Japan, Thursday, July 1, 2021. /Kyodo News via AP The starting pitching dominos are falling in free agency ahead of the expected Dec. 1 lockout, with Skubal serving as the catalyst by signing his nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets . The Blue Jays made a competitive nine-year, $420 million offer for Skuba l, but he opted for $30 million more to head to Flushing. Freddy Peralta agreed to a five-year, $125 million deal with the Orioles on Tuesday, and the pitching-needy Blue Jays swooped in to land the talented 27-year-old Taira. Taira has experience as a reliever and starter, and spent the past season with the Seibu Lions of the Japan Pacific League as a starter. He posted a 1.54 ERA spanning 23 outings, pitching 146 innings and striking out 141 batters. Taira walked 45 batters but allowed just four homers. The year prior, he made 54 appearances and tallied 52 2/3 innings while posting a 2.05 ERA. He owns a career 1.85 ERA in his nine seasons pitching in Japan, according to Baseball Reference. “His stuff and release characteristics are what is intriguing to evaluators. His fastball sits 94-97 mph and hits 100 mph with his four-seam fastball, the headliner in an eight-pitch mix: sinker, changeup, splitter, cutter, slider, sweeper, and curveball,” according to ESPN . “Taira achieves a unique low release and advantageous angle for his fastball with his outlier extension (roughly a foot more than his 5-foot-8 stature) and lower than average arm slot.” The Blue Jays now have a solid rotation featuring AL Cy Young runner-up Dylan Cease, Taira, midseason trade acquisition righty Joel Soriano and talented youngster Trey Yesavage. They reportedly are also in the mix for offensive help and their representatives met with Jazz Chisholm Jr. earlier in free agency. Toronto finished in last place in the AL East last year following its run to the World Series in 2025.

item.title: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions
item.description: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions Fran Soto, president of Spain’s Technical Committee of Referees (CTA), has expressed his desire to improve relations with Real Madrid amid ongoing tensions. Los Blancos have been vociferous in their complaints about the refereeing in Spain as well as the Negreira scandal involving Barcelona, leading to a lot of tension between the club and the governing bodies. Soto wants to move on from the Negreira scandal Speaking to the media at the first Refereeing Gala, Soto addressed the ongoing tensions surrounding the refereeing in Spain and Real Madrid’s complaints, in particular. The CTA president defended the refereeing community over the fallout from the Negreira scandal and called for the focus to shift towards restoring normality. “The referees are the ones most harmed by a person who was vice president of the Technical Committee of Referees,” Soto said, as quoted by SPORT . Real Madrid are unhappy with the refereeing in Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Soto insisted that officials have suffered the consequences of the controversy and argued that they cannot remain trapped by events from the past. ”We mustn’t dwell on the past; we have to move forward and continue refereeing, put it behind us, and look to the future,” he added. Soto questions Real Madrid’s VAR statistics Soto was also asked about the presentation made by Real Madrid during the club’s recent assembly , wherein they showed that VAR had ruled out 42 of their goals since the technology was introduced, compared to 19 for Barcelona. Real Madrid president Florentino Perez used the figures to reinforce the club’s complaints about what it considers unfavourable refereeing treatment. Real Madrid have made multiple complaints over the officiating. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) Soto declined to engage in a direct confrontation with Real Madrid but questioned whether the figures, on their own, could support the conclusions being drawn. “Every club defends its position. I don’t agree that this objective data can be used to draw conclusions,” he stated. However, the CTA president made clear that he has no intention of escalating the dispute and would prefer to see communication between the two sides return to normal. “I don’t want to get into a dispute with any club, least of all with Madrid. I hope that in the future we can resolve this situation,” he concluded.

item.title: IMSA Cuts Testing Days: A Smart Move For The 2027 Season
item.description: The No. 52 LMP2 Inter Europol ORECA of Nick Boulle and Tom Dolman drives through the Carousel during the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Sunday, August 4, 2024, at Road America in Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect IMSA is finally cutting the fat off the testing schedule for the 2027 WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. The new sporting regulations announced Tuesday hit the top teams the hardest, but they might be exactly what the series needs to level the playing field. The rules eliminate all private testing for GTD Pro entries outside of sanctioned events. GTP teams now get only two manufacturer test days per season, with team-specific days removed entirely. According to Sportscar365 , these restrictions come alongside new licensed tests at Sebring and Road Atlanta that are open to every team. The move stops deep-pocketed teams from hoarding track time and forces everyone to rely on their actual race strategy. Inter Europol Doubles Down Anyway While the rulebook tightens, one team is betting big on its own talent. For the 2027 season, Inter Europol Competition revealed plans to run two full-time ORECA LMP2 07 entries. This expansion adds a second car to their existing No. 43 program, creating a formidable two-car assault on the title. The team manager, Sascha Fassbender, said, “We are very happy to have two cars committed to the full IMSA season with two strong driver lineups.” Inter Europol is not backing down from the challenge despite the reduced testing window. The team aims to fight for the championship with both cars, building on a close 2026 title race. Following their second-place finish last year, Jeremy Clarke and Tom Dillmann are back for the flagship No. 43 car. Clarke noted their drive to win, stating, “We came so close last year, so we’re even more motivated to finish on the top step at the end of the season.” Testing Limits Will Test Team Depth The new regulations also slash test days for LMP2 and GTD teams, cutting LMP2 allocation from 12 days down to eight. GTD teams see their days drop from six to two, though FIA Bronze-rated drivers still get two extra days. According to Sportscar365, private testing is now banned during a 120-day blackout period preceding major events like Daytona and Sebring. This forces teams to be sharper with their limited track time. Inter Europol’s new No. 343 entry brings in fresh firepower with drivers Nick Yelloly and Daniel Goldburg. Goldburg brings experience from racing against the team for three years in LMP2. He summed up his move to the organization with a simple phrase: “If you can’t beat them, join them.” The team has also added INDYCAR driver Nolan Siegel for the Rolex 24 at Daytona lineup. The 2027 season will start with a sanctioned test at Daytona International Speedway on December 10 and 11.

item.title: 'It's impossible to make an analysis' - Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca admits Mauricio Pochettino's Man Utd are a mystery ahead of Champions League clash
item.description: Fenerbahce v OL Lyonnes - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play-Offs First Leg - Getty Images Sport Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca says it is "impossible to make an analysis" of Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash in Lisbon. With Leny Yoro sent off after eight minutes at Anfield, Fonseca has turned to footage of Pochettino's time with the United States, while refusing to label the Red Devils "fragile". Fonseca in the dark over Pochettino's United Fonseca has admitted he has little to go on when preparing for United, with Pochettino having taken charge of only one game. That match, a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, was disrupted by Yoro's early red card, which has since been overturned on appeal. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," Fonseca said, as reported by BBC Sport . "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." Fonseca refuses to label United 'fragile' Despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Fonseca refused to accept that they are vulnerable. "I don't follow the reasoning," he said. "Manchester is a great team. I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile." He pointed to United's last Champions League outing, when they came from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day," he added. United's domestic slump United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their last six matches, leaving Pochettino with a huge task after replacing Michael Carrick during the international break. Fonseca, who was appointed on November 4 after Sporting bought him out of his contract at Lyon, is also new to his role and has had little time to stamp his own ideas on the side. Defender Eduardo Quaresma has already warned his team-mates against underestimating United . Lisbon showdown awaits Sporting host United at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday night, with Yoro cleared to play. Pochettino will be desperate for a positive result to ease the pressure after a chaotic start to his reign.

item.title: Detroit Lions lose rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard for the season
item.description: The Detroit Lions have lost another player to a season-ending injury on their defense. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 24, that rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard will miss the rest of the season after injuring his knee in last week’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Gill-Howard was hurt on a goal-line offensive snap, where’s he’s played at times as a jumbo tight end this season, late in the game. “Hate that for him,” Campbell said. “He’s had a heck of a season up to this point.” A sixth-round pick out of Texas Tech, Gill-Howard has played as the Lions’ No. 3 defensive tackle this season and been one of their best interior pass rushers. He has 11 tackles, six quarterback hits and two sacks. Gill-Howard’s injury is the second major setback on the defensive line and third to the unit this month. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell is out for the season with a spinal cord injury he suffered in a Nov. 1 win over the Minnesota Vikings, and Pro Bowl defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore the ACL in his right knee while celebrating a sack in the Lions’ win over the New England Patriots in Germany two weeks ago. Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Gill-Howard have played the bulk of the snaps at defensive tackle for the Lions this season, but Campbell said he’s confident in the team’s depth at the position. Big ends Tyler Lacy and Levi Onwuzurike can play inside, Mekhi Wingo could see his first action of the season and practice squad linemen Aidan Keanaaina and Taki Taimani are candidates to play in the Lions’ Thanksgiving game this week against the Chicago Bears. The centre-back was an unused substitute in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, a result that underlined the scale of the task facing new head coach Mauricio Pochettino. The report states that Heaven is worried about what United’s position in the relegation zone could mean for his progress. This is a player now working under his third manager in 21 months since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025. It is understood he recognises that Pochettino may favour senior options as United attempt to avoid what the report describes as a “shock relegation”. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
